text:
A: Hiya.
B: Now then. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah, fine. You?
B: Yeah. Bit of an echo but it'll do.
A: Okay.
B: So, er, what do you do then? Are we meant to just chat, is that it?
A: I think so, yeah. Erm, I'm a software developer. Payroll software, for councils and NHS trusts mostly.
B: Payroll. So you're the one to blame when my overtime's come through wrong.
A: Probably not, unless you work for a council. But yeah, somebody like me, sort of.
B: No, I'm in a factory, plastics. Injection moulding, I set the machines up. Been there twenty-two year now, before that it were shifts at another place. I'm on permanent days now, which, to be fair, I earned.
A: Right. What do you make?
B: Components. Clips, housings, bits that go in cars and white goods. You'd have a dozen of ours in your kitchen and not know it. I keep my own book of all the settings, because the system's got half of them wrong. Lowest scrap rate on the line, mine.
A: Ha. That's basically my job. Somebody says the system's right and I'm the one who knows it isn't.
B: There you go then. Same thing.
A: Sort of, yeah. Except mine's about thirty years old and held together with sellotape.
B: What, the computer?
A: The code. The payroll engine. Nobody else really understands it, so, erm, they leave me alone mostly. Which suits me.
B: That's job security, that.
A: Until they replace it. They're moving it all to the cloud, whatever that means this week.
B: Hm. They tried to bring in a new system at ours, touch screens on every machine. Lasted about three month, half the lads couldn't use it. Younger ones are worse, stood about on their phones all day.
A: Yeah.
B: Where are you, then? You sound Lancashire.
A: Bolton. You?
B: Hucknall. Nottingham, near enough.
A: Right. Did you do the puzzle thing at the start?
B: I did. Daft, weren't it. I got most of them, mind. Didn't see the point of the ones with the shapes.
A: I just guessed the shape ones tbh. Sorry, I mean I just guessed them, I didn't really think about it.
B: Can't say I blame you. So what d'you do of a weekend, then? You've a dog, I saw the lead.
A: Oh, yeah. Bramble. Cocker spaniel. She's a nightmare, she gets in the bins every single day, I don't know how. I walk her round Moss Bank Park on a Saturday after a bacon barm. That's about as exciting as it gets.
B: Barm. You lot and your barms. It's a cob.
A: It's not a cob, what's a cob?
B: It's a cob, me duck. A bacon cob. Everybody in Nottingham'll tell you.
A: Well, everybody in Bolton'll tell you it's a barm, so.
B: Ha. Fair enough. We had a dog, Labrador. Died two year back. Not getting another, the vet bills were shocking.
A: Oh, sorry. Yeah, they're not cheap. Bramble had her ear done last year and it was, erm, I don't even want to think about it.
B: Insurance went up every year an' all, didn't it.
A: Every year. My husband deals with all that, to be honest, I'd forget to renew it.
B: Mine's the same the other way round, I do all the bills. Julie'd just pay whatever they asked. I rang up last month, knocked forty quid off the car insurance just by asking.
A: Yeah, Mark does that. He's on the phone for an hour, I'd just give up.
B: You've got to, mind. They count on folk not bothering.
